title: The Silent Signal
short: A fictional observation station stops transmitting after its equipment is rearranged.
brief: A fictional school-sponsored night-sky instrument station on an imagined property near Selah stopped sending messages during a demonstration. A power indicator went dark and a toolbox was moved. Students must analyze circuit readings, signal timing, and bench records to determine what interrupted the system. All people and the station are fictional.
caseQuestion: Who changed the power connection, and does the timeline suggest an accidental setup mistake?

sites.label: Fictional observation shelter

clues.title: Voltage drop
clues.detail: The model monitor shows 12 V immediately before interruption and 0 V immediately after. This points to a missing supply at the measurement point.
clues.question: What should be examined first?
options: A visitor list from last week

clues.title: Loose-style socket
clues.detail: The plug fits the adjacent unused receptacle mechanically but its contacts are recessed and do not carry power. The safe practice model contains no live wiring.
clues.question: Why might the instrument go dark?
options: The connector is not electrically engaged

clues.title: Last digital packet
clues.detail: The system recorded its final complete data packet at 8:14:06 and a zero-voltage status at 8:14:07. The events are one second apart.
clues.question: What does the time sequence support?
options: Power loss closely preceded the signal stop

clues.title: Independent archive
clues.detail: The local computer kept previously saved observations. Those files have normal checksums even though new messages stopped.
clues.question: Which conclusion is justified?
options: The connection failed without proving earlier data corruption

clues.title: Detached lead tag
clues.detail: A tag marked BACKUP-12V has fresh adhesive and fits the empty space on the spare cable.
clues.question: How should this clue be used?
options: It helps associate a cable with its intended circuit
It gives an exact voltage at any time

clues.title: Test setup notebook
clues.detail: A written note says backup connection test 8:14. The shared circuit diagram was not updated after an equipment rearrangement.
clues.question: What procedure was missing?
options: A checked and recorded connection change

clues.title: Instrument inspection
clues.detail: No physical damage appears on the instrument’s connector. A simulated continuity check indicates the path from power rack to instrument is open.
clues.question: What is a reasonable technical conclusion?
options: An interruption exists along the supply path
The instrument lens causes all voltage loss

labs.title: Voltage network
labs.story: Adjust supply voltage and compare a simplified output meter reading.
labs.explanation: In the idealized connected model, higher source voltage produces higher meter voltage.
labs.question: Which scientific interpretation is best supported by this model?
options: A connected meter reading depends on voltage.
Voltage identifies who moved a box.
A disconnected wire always shows full voltage.

labs.title: Circuit resistance
labs.story: Adjust resistance and estimate current for a fixed 12 V reference source.
labs.explanation: Ohm’s law describes ideal direct-current circuits; this is a teaching example.
labs.question: Which scientific interpretation is best supported by this model?
options: Higher resistance causes higher current at fixed voltage.
Current decreases as resistance rises at fixed voltage.

labs.title: Data packet timing
labs.story: Adjust sample interval and compare a modeled rate of packets per minute.
labs.explanation: Shorter intervals allow more packet attempts each minute in this simplified model.
labs.question: Which scientific interpretation is best supported by this model?
options: Long intervals create more packets per minute.
Shorter intervals increase the modeled packet rate.

math.prompt: In an ideal circuit a 12 V source is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows (I = V/R)?

explanation: The voltage timeline, signal timestamps, and backup-test note indicate a misplaced lead during an unverified power rerouting. The evidence supports a connection error, not necessarily deliberate damage.

witnesses.name: Casey Rowan
witnesses.statement: I was part of the backup supply test while equipment on the rack was being rearranged. The connectors looked unusually similar.
witnesses.followup: I expected the connections to be checked against the diagram before the demonstration resumed.
witnesses.question: Which observation would test Casey’s connector account?
options: Inspect the physical socket engagement and diagram
Check a star chart for a different date

witnesses.name: Lena Cho
witnesses.statement: I was calling out sky coordinates and did not touch the power rack.
witnesses.followup: My clipboard records the last received signal.
witnesses.question: What record could corroborate Lena’s last-signal time?

witnesses.name: Dev Patel
witnesses.statement: I copied the received data to a separate laptop. I did not change the wiring.
witnesses.followup: The messages stopped at exactly the same timestamp as a voltage drop.
witnesses.question: What do Dev’s saved data files help distinguish?
options: A new transmission failure from lost old data

witnesses.name: Arden Pike
witnesses.statement: I moved the general toolbox to clear the passage, but the power leads stayed connected when I passed.
witnesses.followup: A label fell from the end of the backup lead earlier that night.
witnesses.question: How can Arden’s loose-label claim be checked?
options: Match the tag to the cable and connector

note: Entirely fictional educational case using a real regional place name as setting. No actual person, facility, business, incident, or allegation is represented.
